folds.text: A chatbot answers and stops. An **AI agent** keeps going: it decides its own steps, uses tools, looks at the results, and carries on until the job is done.
Anthropic separates two kinds of system. In a **workflow**, code lays out the steps in advance. In an **agent**, the model directs its own process and its use of tools.
Claude Code is an example. It gathers context, takes an action, checks the result, and repeats. You can interrupt it at any point to steer.
Agents suit open-ended jobs where you cannot predict the steps. They cost more in time and money, and mistakes can pile up, so test them with guardrails.
Anthropic's advice is to start simple. Use the plainest solution that works, and add an agent only when simpler options fall short.
